title: Correlation Geometry of Quantum Sensor Networks: Local-Global Information Flow and Local Privacy
authors: Gong-Chu Li, Lei Chen, Xu-Song Hong, Hua-Qing Xu, Yuancheng Liu, Si-Qi Zhang, Jia-Hao Zhao, Geng Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo
abstract: Quantum sensor networks typically encode N unknown parameters while targeting a single linear combination, rendering the N-1 remaining parameters as nuisance directions. To rigorously quantify estimation precision under such nuisances, we introduce the concept of effective quantum Fisher information (EQFI) and develop an exact EQFI-based phase map that systematically describes the allocation between local and global EQFI. Leveraging this geometric framework, we identify a fundamental bottleneck termed the "barrel effect": the global EQFI is strictly bounded by the weakest weighted local sensing capacity among all nodes. We further establish concrete conditions for saturating this bound. Crucially, this geometric map delineates how the trade-off between local and global EQFI depends dynamically on quantum correlations, and uncovers a counterintuitive "overcorrelated" regime where excessive correlations actively degrade both local and global performance. Finally, we apply the phase map to intrinsic local privacy and identify the condition under which every local parameter is inaccessible while the desired global combination remains estimable. Overall, our work provides a principled methodology for engineering optimal network states in quantum sensing architectures.
summary: This work introduces the Effective Quantum Fisher Information (EQFI) to quantify estimation precision in multi-parameter quantum sensor networks. It develops a phase map revealing that excessive quantum correlations can paradoxically degrade both local and global measurement capabilities. The methodology provides principled guidelines for engineering network states to achieve high global sensitivity while ensuring individual parameters remain locally private.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the trade-off between local and global estimation precision in quantum sensor networks while accounting for nuisance parameters.
main_result: It establishes a fundamental bottleneck, the 'barrel effect,' bounding global Fisher information by the weakest weighted local sensing capacity, and identifies conditions for achieving intrinsic local privacy.
method: The authors develop an exact Effective Quantum Fisher Information (EQFI)-based phase map to geometrically describe how quantum correlations redistribute metrological information between local and global estimates.
model_or_system: The system is a general N-node Quantum Sensor Network (QSN) whose estimation precision is governed by the multiparameter Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM).
key_observables: Effective Quantum Fisher Information (EQFI), Global EQFI ($E_w$), Local EQFI ($E_i$), and correlation parameters ($\mu_i, s_i, r_i$).
important_parameters: The optimal correlation strength $\mu^*_i$ defining the transition from beneficial to detrimental correlations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the QFIM is nonsingular for core derivations; local privacy is defined as a QFIM-level non-identifiability condition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the information flow, mapping the trade-off between local and global EQFI across different correlation regimes, including an over-correlated penalty zone.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing EQFI, developing the phase map to analyze the local-global trade-off (including the 'barrel effect'), and finally applying this geometry to derive conditions for intrinsic local privacy.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous geometric framework for understanding how quantum correlations can either enhance or actively degrade sensing performance, offering design principles for optimal network states.
